legend: Thanos sort is one of the sorting algorithms that works in time linear in the length of the array.
The sorting algorithm is as follows:
1) If the array a=(a1,⋯,an)%%ZSMJ0%% is already sorted, then the process stops. An array is considered sorted if for every i%%ZSMJ1%% from 2%%ZSMJ2%% to n%%ZSMJ3%%, it holds that ai−1≤ai%%ZSMJ4%%.
2) Otherwise, either the first ⌈n2⌉%%ZSMJ5%% elements of the array or the last ⌊n2⌋%%ZSMJ6%% elements are chosen uniformly at random. All of them are removed, and the algorithm proceeds to step 1.
For example, sorting the array [10,4,5,6,8]%%ZSMJ7%% may look as follows:
Since many elements may disappear during Thanos sort, for an array a%%ZSMJ14%%, let f(a)%%ZSMJ15%% be the expected number of elements remaining in the final array.
You are given some array a%%ZSMJ16%%.

After each query, you need to output f(a)%%ZSMJ19%% for the current array.
input: The first line contains two integers n,q%%ZSMJ20%% (1≤n,q≤106%%ZSMJ21%%) – the length of the array and the number of queries, respectively.
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ22%% integers a1,a2,…,an(0≤ai≤109)%%ZSMJ23%% – the initial values of the array a%%ZSMJ24%%.
Each of the next q%%ZSMJ25%% lines contains a pair of integers i,x%%ZSMJ26%% (1≤i≤n,0≤x≤109%%ZSMJ27%%) – the parameters of the next query.
output: After each query, output f(a)%%ZSMJ28%% modulo 998244353%%ZSMJ29%% on a separate line.
